title: Korean BBQ Pear Bulgogi Sauce
description: Asian pear, sesame and garlic make a savory-sweet bulgogi-style finishing sauce with enough body to coat thin slices of beef.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: peeled Asian pear puree
ingredients.note: Grate or blend a peeled ripe Asian pear until smooth.

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef broth
ingredients.note: Use plain unsalted beef broth at about 60 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 2 tsp total.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

steps.title: Cook the pear
steps.text: Simmer {pr}, {be}, {ga} and {gi} in the HexClad for 5 minutes, stirring so the pear stays off the bottom.

steps.title: Balance the barbecue base
steps.text: Whisk in {a}, {bs}, {pep} and {so}. Simmer for 2 minutes, then blend until smooth if the pear is still coarse.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon onto cooked thin beef or chicken, especially meat finished under a Blackstone dome. Serve extra sauce with rice.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 2 tsp coconut aminos in place of 6 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, halve the garlic and omit the black pepper. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 49 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 9.1 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.8 g fiber, 144 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 44 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 7.8 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.8 g fiber, 54 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
